#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Script to extract Python documentation sitemap structure
"""

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import json

BASE_URL = "https://docs.python.org/3"

def get_sections_from_contents():
    """Extract main sections from the contents page"""
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/contents.html"
    try:
        response = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(response.content, 'html.parser')
        
        # Find the main content list
        main_div = soup.find('main', role='main')
        if not main_div:
            main_div = soup.find('div', {'class': 'body'})
        
        structure = []
        
        # Find the top-level list
        top_list = main_div.find('ul', recursive=False) if main_div else None
        if not top_list:
            top_list = main_div.find('ul') if main_div else None
            
        if top_list:
            # Get all main sections (level 1)
            for li in top_list.find_all('li', recursive=False):
                section_data = parse_section(li)
                if section_data:
                    structure.append(section_data)
        
        return structure
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}")
        return []

def parse_section(li_tag, level=0):
    """Parse a section and its subsections"""
    # Get the first link (section title)
    link = li_tag.find('a', recursive=False)
    
    if link:
        title = link.get_text(strip=True)
        href = link.get('href', '')
        
        # Skip if no title or just a bullet
        if not title or title in ['•', '◦', '■']:
            return None
        
        body_text = li_tag.find(string=True, recursive=False)
        
        section = {
            'title': title,
            'url': f"{BASE_URL}/{href}" if href else '',
            'level': level,
            'subsections': []
        }
        
        # Find nested list in this li
        nested_list = li_tag.find('ul', recursive=False)
        if nested_list:
            for sub_li in nested_list.find_all('li', recursive=False):
                sub = parse_section(sub_li, level + 1)
                if sub:
                    section['subsections'].append(sub)
        
        return section
    return None

def filter_major_sections(structure):
    """Filter only the major documentation sections"""
    major_sections = []
    
    # Define important section keywords
    key_sections = [
        "What's New", "Tutorial", "Library", "Language Reference",
        "Setup", "Installing", "Distributing", "Extending", "C API",
        "HOWTO", "FAQ", "Deprecations", "Glossary", "About"
    ]
    
    for section in structure:
        title = section.get('title', '')
        # Check if this is a major section
        for key in key_sections:
            if key.lower() in title.lower():
                section['type'] = 'major'
                major_sections.append(section)
                break
        else:
            # Check if it has many subsections (might be important)
            if len(section.get('subsections', [])) > 5:
                section['type'] = 'major'
                major_sections.append(section)
    
    return major_sections

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Fetching Python documentation sitemap...")
    structure = get_sections_from_contents()
    
    print(f"\nFound {len(structure)} main sections")
    
    # Print major sections with summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PYTHON 3 DOCUMENTATION SITEMAP")
    print("="*80)
    
    major = filter_major_sections(structure)
    
    for i, section in enumerate(structure, 1):
        sub_count = len(section.get('subsections', []))
        print(f"\n{i}. {section['title']}")
        if sub_count > 0:
            print(f"   └─ {sub_count} subsections")
            # Show first few subsections
            for j, sub in enumerate(section['subsections'][:5], 1):
                print(f"      {j}. {sub['title'][:60]}")
            if sub_count > 5:
                print(f"      ... ({sub_count - 5} more)")

        json.dump(structure[:20], f, indent=2)

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re

headers = {'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36'}
response = requests.get('https://github.com/trending/python', headers=headers)
soup = BeautifulSoup(response.content, 'html.parser')

articles = soup.find_all('article')

for i, article in enumerate(articles[:10], 1):
    # Repository name
    repo_link = article.find('h2')
    if repo_link:
        repo_name = repo_link.get_text(strip=True).replace('\n', '').replace(' ', '')
    else:
        repo_name = 'N/A'
    
    # Description
    desc_p = article.find('p')
    description = desc_p.get_text(strip=True) if desc_p else 'No description'
    
    # Get all links in the article
    all_links = article.find_all('a')
    stars = forks = '0'
    for link in all_links:
        text = link.get_text(strip=True)
        # Look for star count
        if text and any(c.isdigit() for c in text):
            if 'star' in link.get('href', '') or 'stargazers' in link.get('href', ''):
                stars = text
            elif 'fork' in link.get('href', '') or 'forks' in link.get('href', ''):
                forks = text
    
    # Today's stars - look for the span with 'stars today'
    all_text = article.get_text()
    today_match = re.search(r'(\d+(?:,\d+)*)\s+stars?\s+today', all_text)
    today_stars = today_match.group(0) if today_match else 'N/A'
    
    print(f'{i}. {repo_name}')
    print(f'   Description: {description}')
    print(f'   Stars: {stars} | Forks: {forks}')
    print(f'   Trending: {today_stars}')
    print()

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import json
from datetime import datetime

# Scrape PyPI Blog for article metadata
def scrape_pypi_blog():
    url = "https://blog.pypi.org/"
    headers = {
        'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36'
    }
    
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.content, 'html.parser')
    
    articles = []
    
    # Find all article elements
    article_elements = soup.find_all('article')
    
    for article in article_elements:
        # Extract title
        title_elem = article.find('h2')
        title = title_elem.get_text(strip=True) if title_elem else None
        
        # Extract link
        title_link = article.find('h2').find('a') if title_elem else None
        link = None
        if title_link:
            href = title_link.get('href', '')
            if href.startswith('/'):
                link = f"https://blog.pypi.org{href}"
            else:
                link = href
        
        # Extract date
        time_elem = article.find('time')
        date = time_elem.get_text(strip=True) if time_elem else None
        
        # Extract read time
        read_time_elem = article.find_all('li')
        read_time = None
        for li in read_time_elem:
            text = li.get_text(strip=True)
            if 'min read' in text or 'read' in text:
                read_time = text
                break
        
        # Extract author
        author_elem = article.find('img')
        author = author_elem.get('alt', '') if author_elem else None
        
        # Extract summary/excerpt
        summary = None
        if article.find('p'):
            summary = article.find('p').get_text(strip=True)
        
        article_data = {
            'title': title,
            'url': link,
            'author': author,
            'published_date': date,
            'read_time': read_time,
            'summary': summary,
            'source': 'PyPI Blog'
        }
        
        # Only add if we have at least a title
        if title:
            articles.append(article_data)
    
    return articles

# Scrape PyPI main page for general statistics
def scrape_pypi_main():
    url = "https://pypi.org/"
    headers = {
        'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36'
    }
    
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.content, 'html.parser')
    
    stats = {}
    
    # Extract statistics
    stat_paragraphs = soup.find_all('p')
    for p in stat_paragraphs:
        text = p.get_text(strip=True)
        if 'projects' in text:
            stats['total_projects'] = text
        elif 'releases' in text:
            stats['total_releases'] = text
        elif 'files' in text:
            stats['total_files'] = text
        elif 'users' in text:
            stats['total_users'] = text
    
    return stats

# Main execution
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Scraping PyPI Blog...")
    blog_articles = scrape_pypi_blog()
    
    print("Scraping PyPI Main Page...")
    pypi_stats = scrape_pypi_main()
    
    full_data = {
        'metadata': {
            'scraped_at': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'source': 'https://blog.pypi.org/',
            'source_name': 'PyPI Blog'
        },
        'pypi_statistics': pypi_stats,
        'articles': blog_articles
    }
    
    # Output as JSON
    output_json = json.dumps(full_data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    print(output_json)
    
    # Save to file
    with open('pypi_articles_metadata.json', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(output_json)
    
    print(f"\n✅ Successfully scraped {len(blog_articles)} articles!")
    print("📁 Data saved to 'pypi_articles_metadata.json'")

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re

def scrape_books():
    base_url = "https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/page-{}.html"
    books = []
    
    # There are 50 pages total (1000 books, 20 per page)
    for page in range(1, 51):
        url = base_url.format(page)
        response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(response.content, 'html.parser')
        
        # Find all book articles
        articles = soup.find_all('article', class_='product_pod')
        
        for article in articles:
            # Get title
            title = article.h3.a['title']
            
            # Get price - convert to float
            price_text = article.find('p', class_='price_color').text
            price = float(re.sub(r'[^0-9.]', '', price_text))
            
            # Get rating class to determine number of stars
            rating_class = article.find('p', class_='star-rating')['class']
            rating_map = {
                'One': 1,
                'Two': 2,
                'Three': 3,
                'Four': 4,
                'Five': 5
            }
            rating = rating_map.get([c for c in rating_class if c in rating_map][0], 0)
            
            # Get availability
            availability = article.find('p', class_='instock availability').text.strip()
            
            books.append({
                'title': title,
                'price': price,
                'rating': rating,
                'availability': availability
            })
    
    return books

books = scrape_books()
print(f"Found {len(books)} books")

# Sort by price and rating to find best-priced books with good ratings
# Filter for 4+ star ratings and sort by price
high_rated = [b for b in books if b['rating'] >= 4]
high_rated_sorted = sorted(high_rated, key=lambda x: (x['rating'], -x['price']), reverse=True)

# Get top 10 best value books (low price + high rating)
print("\n=== Top 10 Best-Value Books (High Rating + Low Price) ===")
for i, book in enumerate(high_rated_sorted[:10], 1):
    print(f"{i}. {book['title']}")
    print(f"   Price: £{book['price']:.2f} | Rating: {book['rating']} stars")
    print()

# Lowest priced books with 5 stars
five_star = [b for b in books if b['rating'] == 5]
five_star_sorted = sorted(five_star, key=lambda x: x['price'])

print("\n=== Cheapest 5-Star Books ===")

# JSONPlaceholder Documentation
## Free Fake REST API for Testing and Prototyping

---

## Overview

JSONPlaceholder is a free online REST API that provides fake data for testing and prototyping. It's powered by JSON Server and LowDB, serving ~3 billion requests each month.

**Base URL:** `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com`

---

## Resources

JSONPlaceholder comes with a set of 6 common resources:

| Resource      | Count |
|---------------|-------|
| `/posts`      | 100 posts |
| `/comments`   | 500 comments |
| `/albums`     | 100 albums |
| `/photos`     | 5000 photos |
| `/todos`      | 200 todos |
| `/users`      | 10 users |

**Note:** Resources have relations. For example:
- Posts have many comments
- Albums have many photos
- Users have albums, todos, and posts

---

## Routes

All HTTP methods are supported. You can use `http` or `https` for your requests.

### Available HTTP Methods

| Method   | Endpoint                      | Description              |
|----------|-------------------------------|--------------------------|
| GET      | `/posts`                      | List all posts           |
| GET      | `/posts/1`                    | Get a specific post      |
| GET      | `/posts/1/comments`           | Get comments for a post  |
| GET      | `/comments?postId=1`          | Filter comments by post  |
| POST     | `/posts`                      | Create a new post        |
| PUT      | `/posts/1`                    | Update a post (full)     |
| PATCH    | `/posts/1`                    | Update a post (partial)  |
| DELETE   | `/posts/1`                    | Delete a post            |

---

## Guide & Usage Examples

### Getting a Resource

```javascript
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1')
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

**Output:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "...",
  "body": "...",
  "userId": 1
}
```

### Listing All Resources

```javascript
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts')
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

**Output:**
```json
[
  { "id": 1, "title": "..." },
  { "id": 2, "title": "..." },
  { "id": 3, "title": "..." },
  /* ... */
  { "id": 100, "title": "..." }
]
```

### Creating a Resource

```javascript
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    title: 'foo',
    body: 'bar',
    userId: 1,
  }),
  headers: {
    'Content-type': 'application/json; charset=UTF-8',
  },
})
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

**Output:**
```json
{
  "id": 101,
  "title": "foo",
  "body": "bar",
  "userId": 1
}
```

**⚠️ Important:** The resource will not actually be created on the server, but it will be faked as if it was.

### Updating a Resource (PUT)

```javascript
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1', {
  method: 'PUT',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    id: 1,
    title: 'foo',
    body: 'bar',
    userId: 1,
  }),
  headers: {
    'Content-type': 'application/json; charset=UTF-8',
  },
})
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

**Output:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "foo",
  "body": "bar",
  "userId": 1
}
```

**⚠️ Important:** The resource will not actually be updated on the server, but it will be faked as if it was.

### Patching a Resource (PATCH)

```javascript
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1', {
  method: 'PATCH',
  body: JSON.stringify({
    title: 'foo',
  }),
  headers: {
    'Content-type': 'application/json; charset=UTF-8',
  },
})
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

**Output:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "foo",
  "body": "...",
  "userId": 1
}
```

**⚠️ Important:** The resource will not actually be updated on the server, but it will be faked as if it was.

### Deleting a Resource

```javascript
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1', {
  method: 'DELETE',
});
```

**⚠️ Important:** The resource will not actually be deleted on the server, but it will be faked as if it was.

### Filtering Resources

Basic filtering is supported through query parameters:

```javascript
// This will return all the posts that belong to the first user
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts?userId=1')
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

### Listing Nested Resources

One level of nested routes is available:

```javascript
// This is equivalent to /comments?postId=1
fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1/comments')
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((json) => console.log(json));
```

**Available Nested Routes:**
- `/posts/1/comments`
- `/albums/1/photos`
- `/users/1/albums`
- `/users/1/todos`
- `/users/1/posts`

import json

    base_url = 'https://books.toscrape.com/'
    books_data = []
    current_page = 1
    
    while True:
        print(f"Scraping page {current_page}...")
        
        # Determine URL based on page number
        if current_page == 1:
            url = base_url + 'index.html'
        else:
            url = base_url + f'catalogue/page-{current_page}.html'
        
        # Fetch the page
        response = requests.get(url)
        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Failed to fetch page {current_page}: {response.status_code}")
            break
        
        soup = BeautifulSoup(response.content, 'html.parser')
        
        # Find all book articles
        articles = soup.find_all('article', class_='product_pod')
        
        if not articles:
            print("No more books found.")
            break
        
        for article in articles:
            # Title
            title_elem = article.find('h3').find('a') if article.find('h3') else None
            title = title_elem.get('title') if title_elem else None
            link = title_elem.get('href') if title_elem else None
            
            # Image URL
            img_elem = article.find('img', class_='thumbnail')
            image_url = img_elem.get('src') if img_elem else None
            
            # Price
            price_elem = article.find('p', class_='price_color')
            price = price_elem.get_text() if price_elem else None
            
            # Availability
            avail_elem = article.find('p', class_='instock availability')
            availability = avail_elem.get_text().strip() if avail_elem else None
            
            # Rating
            rating_elem = article.find('p', class_='star-rating')
            rating = None
            if rating_elem:
                classes = rating_elem.get('class', [])
                for c in classes:
                    if c != 'star-rating':
                        rating = c
                        break
            
            # Fix relative URLs
            if link and not link.startswith('http'):
                if link.startswith('../'):
                    link = base_url + 'catalogue/' + link[3:]
                else:
                    link = base_url + 'catalogue/' + link
            
            if image_url and not image_url.startswith('http'):
                if image_url.startswith('../'):
                    image_url = base_url + image_url[3:]
                else:
                    image_url = base_url + image_url
            
            books_data.append({
                'title': title,
                'link': link,
                'image_url': image_url,
                'price': price,
                'availability': availability,
                'rating': rating
            })
        
        # Check for next page
        next_page = soup.find('li', class_='next')
        if not next_page:
            break
        
        current_page += 1
        time.sleep(0.5)  # Be polite to the server
    
    return books_data

if __name__ == '__main__':
    books = scrape_books()
    print(f"\nTotal books scraped: {len(books)}")
    
    # Save to JSON

async def list_users(

    page: int = Query(1, ge=1, description="Page number"),
    per_page: int = Query(20, ge=1, le=100, description="Items per page"),
    search: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Search by name or email"),
    is_active: Optional[bool] = Query(None, description="Filter by active status")
):
    """List users with pagination and filtering"""
    request_id = getattr(request.state, 'request_id', 'unknown')
    
    # Filter users
    filtered = list(_users_db.values())
    
    if search:
        filtered = [u for u in filtered if search.lower() in u.full_name.lower() or search in u.email]
    
    if is_active is not None:
        filtered = [u for u in filtered if u.is_active == is_active]
    
    # Pagination
    total = len(filtered)
    start = (page - 1) * per_page
    end = start + per_page
    paginated = filtered[start:end]
    
    total_pages = (total + per_page - 1) // per_page
    
    return APIResponse(
        data=paginated,
        meta=PaginationMeta(
            total=total,
            page=page,
            per_page=per_page,
            total_pages=total_pages,
            has_next=page < total_pages,

    results["issues"].append({
        "severity": "CRITICAL",
        "category": "Security",
        "description": "Debug mode enabled in production"
    })
    results["summary"]["critical_issues"] += 1

    results["issues"].append({
        "severity": "CRITICAL",
        "category": "Security",
        "description": "No input validation on user inputs"
    })
    results["summary"]["critical_issues"] += 1

# Global state
if "global db_connection" in content:
    results["issues"].append({
        "severity": "WARNING",
        "category": "Code Quality",

#!/bin/bash
#
# Advanced Parallel Build Script
# Runs multiple build commands in parallel with result collection
#

set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
MAX_JOBS=3
LOG_DIR="logs"
RESULTS_FILE="build-results.json"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Create log directory
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

# Define builds: name|command|logfile
declare -a BUILDS=(
    "frontend|./frontend/build.sh|$LOG_DIR/frontend-advanced.log"
    "backend|./backend/build.sh|$LOG_DIR/backend-advanced.log"
    "docs|./docs/build.sh|$LOG_DIR/docs-advanced.log"
)

# Results tracking
declare -A START_TIMES
declare -A END_TIMES
declare -A STATUSES
declare -A PIDS

echo "Starting parallel build with max $MAX_JOBS concurrent jobs..."
echo ""

# Function to run a single build
run_build() {
    local name="$1"
    local cmd="$2"
    local logfile="$3"
    
    START_TIMES[$name]=$(date +%s)
    echo "[$name] Starting at $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
    
    if eval "$cmd" > "$logfile" 2>&1; then
        STATUSES[$name]=0
        echo "[$name] Completed successfully"
    else
        STATUSES[$name]=$?
        echo "[$name] Failed with exit code ${STATUSES[$name]}"
    fi
    
    END_TIMES[$name]=$(date +%s)
}

# Run all builds in parallel
for build in "${BUILDS[@]}"; do
    IFS='|' read -r name cmd logfile <<< "$build"
    run_build "$name" "$cmd" "$logfile" &
    PIDS[$name]=$!
done

# Wait for all builds
echo ""
echo "Waiting for all builds to complete..."
echo ""

for name in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
    wait ${PIDS[$name]}
    END_TIMES[$name]=$(date +%s)
done

# Generate Results Report
echo "========================================="
echo "BUILD RESULTS REPORT"
echo "========================================="
echo ""

TOTAL_SUCCESS=0
TOTAL_FAILED=0

for name in frontend backend docs; do
    status="${STATUSES[$name]:-1}"
    start="${START_TIMES[$name]:-0}"
    end="${END_TIMES[$name]:-0}"
    duration=$((end - start))
    
    if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf "${GREEN}✓${NC} %-10s SUCCESS  (${duration}s)\n" "$name"
        TOTAL_SUCCESS=$((TOTAL_SUCCESS + 1))
    else
        printf "${RED}✗${NC} %-10s FAILED   (exit $status, ${duration}s)\n" "$name"
        TOTAL_FAILED=$((TOTAL_FAILED + 1))
    fi
done

echo ""
echo "========================================="
echo "Summary: $TOTAL_SUCCESS passed, $TOTAL_FAILED failed"
echo "========================================="

# Output results as JSON
cat > "$RESULTS_FILE" << JSON

  "build_timestamp": "$(date -Iseconds)",
  "total_builds": 3,
  "successful": $TOTAL_SUCCESS,
  "failed": $TOTAL_FAILED,
  "results": {
    "frontend": {
      "status": "$(if [ "${STATUSES[frontend]:-1}" -eq 0 ]; then echo "success"; else echo "failed"; fi)",
      "duration_seconds": $((END_TIMES[frontend] - START_TIMES[frontend]))
    },
    "backend": {
      "status": "$(if [ "${STATUSES[backend]:-1}" -eq 0 ]; then echo "success"; else echo "failed"; fi)",
      "duration_seconds": $((END_TIMES[backend] - START_TIMES[backend]))

    "docs": {
      "status": "$(if [ "${STATUSES[docs]:-1}" -eq 0 ]; then echo "success"; else echo "failed"; fi)",
      "duration_seconds": $((END_TIMES[docs] - START_TIMES[docs]))
    }
  }
}
JSON

echo "Results saved to: $RESULTS_FILE"

if [ $TOTAL_FAILED -eq 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "🎉 All builds completed successfully!"
    exit 0

    echo ""
    echo "⚠️  Some builds failed!"

@dataclass
class CacheStats:
    hits: int = 0
    misses: int = 0
    evictions: int = 0
    accesses: int = 0
    
    @property
    def hit_rate(self):
        return self.hits / max(self.accesses, 1)
    
    @property
    def miss_rate(self):
        return self.misses / max(self.accesses, 1)

class BaseCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cache = {}
        self.stats = CacheStats()
    
    def get(self, key):
        raise NotImplementedError
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        raise NotImplementedError
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f\"{self.__class__.__name__}(capacity={self.capacity}, items={len(self.cache)})\"

class LRUCache(BaseCache):
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        super().__init__(capacity)
        self.order = OrderedDict()
    
    def get(self, key):
        self.stats.accesses += 1
        if key in self.cache:
            self.stats.hits += 1
            self.order.move_to_end(key)
            return self.cache[key]
        self.stats.misses += 1
        return None
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.order.move_to_end(key)
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                evicted = next(iter(self.order))
                del self.cache[evicted]
                del self.order[evicted]
                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.order[key] = None

class LFUCache(BaseCache):
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        super().__init__(capacity)
        self.freq = defaultdict(int)
    
    def get(self, key):
        self.stats.accesses += 1
        if key in self.cache:
            self.stats.hits += 1
            self.freq[key] += 1
            return self.cache[key]
        self.stats.misses += 1
        return None
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.freq[key] += 1
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                min_freq_keys = [k for k, v in self.freq.items() if v == min(self.freq.values())]
                evicted = min_freq_keys[0]
                del self.cache[evicted]
                del self.freq[evicted]
                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.freq[key] = 1

class FIFOCache(BaseCache):
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        super().__init__(capacity)
        self.queue = []
    
    def get(self, key):
        self.stats.accesses += 1
        if key in self.cache:
            self.stats.hits += 1
            return self.cache[key]
        self.stats.misses += 1
        return None
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache[key] = value
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                evicted = self.queue.pop(0)
                del self.cache[evicted]
                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.queue.append(key)

class RandomCache(BaseCache):
    def get(self, key):
        self.stats.accesses += 1
        if key in self.cache:
            self.stats.hits += 1
            return self.cache[key]
        self.stats.misses += 1
        return None
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache[key] = value
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                evicted = random.choice(list(self.cache.keys()))
                del self.cache[evicted]
                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value

class WorkloadGenerator:
    @staticmethod
    def uniform(num_items: int, num_accesses: int) -> List[int]:
        return [random.randint(0, num_items - 1) for _ in range(num_accesses)]
    
    @staticmethod
    def zipfian(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, alpha: float = 1.0) -> List[int]:
        zipf = np.random.zipf(alpha, num_accesses)
        return [min(x % num_items, num_items - 1) for x in zipf]
    
    @staticmethod
    def sequential(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, loop: bool = True) -> List[int]:
        pattern = list(range(min(num_items, num_accesses)))
        if loop:
            pattern = (pattern * (num_accesses // len(pattern) + 1))[:num_accesses]
        return pattern
    
    @staticmethod
    def temporal_locality(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, locality_ratio: float = 0.8) -> List[int]:
        working_set_size = int(num_items * 0.2)
        pattern = []
        for i in range(num_accesses):
            if random.random() < locality_ratio and pattern:
                recent_start = max(0, len(pattern) - working_set_size)
                pattern.append(random.choice(pattern[recent_start:]))
            else:
                pattern.append(random.randint(0, num_items - 1))
        return pattern
    
    @staticmethod
    def cyclic_shift(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, cycle_size: int = None) -> List[int]:
        if cycle_size is None:
            cycle_size = num_items // 4
        pattern = []
        for i in range(num_accesses):
            cycle = (i // cycle_size) % (num_items // cycle_size + 1)
            offset = i % cycle_size
            pattern.append((cycle * cycle_size + offset) % num_items)
        return pattern

    for key in workload:
        if cache.get(key) is None:
            cache.put(key, f\"value_{key}\")
    return cache.stats

    if labels is None:
        labels = [c.__class__.__name__ for c in caches]
    
    results = []
    for cache, label in zip(caches, labels):
        cache.stats = CacheStats()
        cache.cache.clear()
        if hasattr(cache, 'order'):
            cache.order.clear()
        if hasattr(cache, 'freq'):
            cache.freq.clear()
        if hasattr(cache, 'queue'):
            cache.queue.clear()
        
        stats = run_simulation(cache, workload)
        results.append({
            'Strategy': label,
            'Hit Rate': stats.hit_rate,
            'Miss Rate': stats.miss_rate,
            'Hits': stats.hits,
            'Misses': stats.misses,
            'Evictions': stats.evictions,
            'Total Accesses': stats.accesses
        })
    
    return pd.DataFrame(results)

                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.freq[key] = 1

class FIFOCache(BaseCache):
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        super().__init__(capacity)
        self.queue = []
    
    def get(self, key):
        self.stats.accesses += 1
        if key in self.cache:
            self.stats.hits += 1
            return self.cache[key]
        self.stats.misses += 1
        return None
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache[key] = value
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                evicted = self.queue.pop(0)
                del self.cache[evicted]
                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value
            self.queue.append(key)

class RandomCache(BaseCache):
    def get(self, key):
        self.stats.accesses += 1
        if key in self.cache:
            self.stats.hits += 1
            return self.cache[key]
        self.stats.misses += 1
        return None
    
    def put(self, key, value):
        if key in self.cache:
            self.cache[key] = value
        else:
            if len(self.cache) >= self.capacity:
                evicted = random.choice(list(self.cache.keys()))
                del self.cache[evicted]
                self.stats.evictions += 1
            self.cache[key] = value

class WorkloadGenerator:
    @staticmethod
    def uniform(num_items: int, num_accesses: int) -> List[int]:
        return [random.randint(0, num_items - 1) for _ in range(num_accesses)]
    
    @staticmethod
    def zipfian(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, alpha: float = 1.5) -> List[int]:
        zipf = np.random.zipf(alpha, num_accesses)
        return [min(x % num_items, num_items - 1) for x in zipf]
    
    @staticmethod
    def sequential(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, loop: bool = True) -> List[int]:
        pattern = list(range(min(num_items, num_accesses)))
        if loop:
            pattern = (pattern * (num_accesses // len(pattern) + 1))[:num_accesses]
        return pattern
    
    @staticmethod
    def temporal_locality(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, locality_ratio: float = 0.8) -> List[int]:
        working_set_size = int(num_items * 0.2)
        pattern = []
        for i in range(num_accesses):
            if random.random() < locality_ratio and pattern:
                recent_start = max(0, len(pattern) - working_set_size)
                pattern.append(random.choice(pattern[recent_start:]))
            else:
                pattern.append(random.randint(0, num_items - 1))
        return pattern
    
    @staticmethod
    def cyclic_shift(num_items: int, num_accesses: int, cycle_size: int = None) -> List[int]:
        if cycle_size is None:
            cycle_size = num_items // 4
        pattern = []
        for i in range(num_accesses):
            cycle = (i // cycle_size) % (num_items // cycle_size + 1)
            offset = i % cycle_size
            pattern.append((cycle * cycle_size + offset) % num_items)
        return pattern

def run_simulation(cache: BaseCache, workload: List[int]) -> CacheStats:
    for key in workload:
        if cache.get(key) is None:
            cache.put(key, f\"value_{key}\")
    return cache.stats

def compare_caches(caches: List[BaseCache], workload: List[int], labels: List[str] = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if labels is None:
        labels = [c.__class__.__name__ for c in caches]
    
    results = []
    for cache, label in zip(caches, labels):
        cache.stats = CacheStats()
        cache.cache.clear()
        if hasattr(cache, 'order'):
            cache.order.clear()
        if hasattr(cache, 'freq'):
            cache.freq.clear()
        if hasattr(cache, 'queue'):
            cache.queue.clear()
        
        stats = run_simulation(cache, workload)
        results.append({
            'Strategy': label,
            'Hit Rate': stats.hit_rate,
            'Miss Rate': stats.miss_rate,
            'Hits': stats.hits,
            'Misses': stats.misses,
            'Evictions': stats.evictions,
            'Total Accesses': stats.accesses
        })
    
    return pd.DataFrame(results)

# Async Programming Research

## 1. Core Concepts
- Event Loop: The heart of async programming that manages and distributes events
- Coroutines: Functions declared with `async def` that can suspend/resume execution
- Futures/Promises: Objects representing eventual completion of an operation
- Tasks: Units of work scheduled on the event loop
- Concurrency vs Parallelism: Async enables concurrency on a single thread

## 2. Python Async Patterns
```python
# Basic async/await
async def main():
    result = await some_async_function()
    return result

# Concurrent execution with asyncio.gather()
results = await asyncio.gather(task1(), task2(), task3())

# Task creation
asyncio.create_task(coro())  # Fire-and-forget with reference

# Async context managers
async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
    async with session.get(url) as response:
        data = await response.text()
```

## 3. Best Practices
- DON'T: Use `asyncio.run()` inside async functions (already in event loop)
- DON'T: Block the event loop (time.sleep, heavy computation without executor)
- DO: Use `await asyncio.backoff` or asyncio.wait_for() for timeouts
- DO: Clean up resources with async context managers
- DO: Propagate cancellation properly with try/finally or contextlib.aclosing

## 4. Libraries Performance Comparison
| Library | Use Case | Concurrent Connections | Overhead |
|---------|----------|----------------------|----------|
| aiohttp | HTTP Client/Server | 1000s | Low |
| asyncio | Core async primitives | N/A | Minimal |
| trio | Structured concurrency | N/A | Low |
| anyio | Abstraction layer | N/A | Medium |
| uvloop | Fast event loop | Same as asyncio | Very Low (Cython) |

## 5. Common Anti-Patterns & Solutions
- Deadlocks with locks: Use asyncio.Lock() not threading.Lock()
- Losing exceptions: Always await tasks or add done callbacks
- Unbounded growth: Use asyncio.Semaphore to limit concurrency
- Memory leaks: Properly close generators and cancel background tasks

## 6. Real-World Architecture Patterns
- Worker Queue: asyncio.Queue for producer/consumer patterns
- Connection Pooling: Built into most async libraries (aiopg, aioredis)
- Circuit Breaker: Wrap async calls with timeout + retry logic
- Graceful Shutdown: Cancel tasks, wait with timeout, force close

"""
Tests for the main FastAPI application.
"""
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient


def test_root_endpoint(client: TestClient):
    """Test the root endpoint returns welcome message."""
    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert data["message"] == "Welcome to Sample API"
    assert data["version"] == "0.1.0"


def test_health_check(client: TestClient):
    """Test the health check endpoint."""
    response = client.get("/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"status": "healthy"}


class TestItemsEndpoints:
    """Tests for the items CRUD endpoints."""

    def test_list_items_empty(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test listing items returns empty list when no items exist."""
        response = client.get("/items")
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.json() == []

    def test_create_item(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test creating a new item."""
        item_data = {
            "name": "Test Item",
            "description": "A test item",
            "price": 19.99
        }
        response = client.post("/items", json=item_data)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        assert data["id"] == 1
        assert data["name"] == "Test Item"
        assert data["description"] == "A test item"
        assert data["price"] == 19.99

    def test_create_item_without_description(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test creating an item without optional description."""
        item_data = {
            "name": "Simple Item",
            "price": 5.99
        }
        response = client.post("/items", json=item_data)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        assert data["id"] == 1
        assert data["name"] == "Simple Item"
        assert data["description"] is None
        assert data["price"] == 5.99

    def test_get_item(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test getting a single item by ID."""
        # First create an item
        item_data = {"name": "Test Item", "price": 10.0}
        create_response = client.post("/items", json=item_data)
        item_id = create_response.json()["id"]

        # Then retrieve it
        response = client.get(f"/items/{item_id}")
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        assert data["id"] == item_id
        assert data["name"] == "Test Item"

    def test_get_item_not_found(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test getting a non-existent item returns 404."""
        response = client.get("/items/999")
        assert response.status_code == 404
        assert response.json()["detail"] == "Item not found"

    def test_list_items_with_data(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test listing items returns created items."""
        # Create multiple items
        client.post("/items", json={"name": "Item 1", "price": 10.0})
        client.post("/items", json={"name": "Item 2", "price": 20.0})

        response = client.get("/items")
        assert response.status_code == 200
        items = response.json()
        assert len(items) == 2
        assert items[0]["name"] == "Item 1"
        assert items[1]["name"] == "Item 2"

    def test_update_item(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test updating an existing item."""
        # Create an item first
        item_data = {"name": "Original", "price": 10.0}
        create_response = client.post("/items", json=item_data)
        item_id = create_response.json()["id"]

        # Update it
        update_data = {"name": "Updated", "price": 15.0}
        response = client.put(f"/items/{item_id}", json=update_data)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        assert data["id"] == item_id
        assert data["name"] == "Updated"
        assert data["price"] == 15.0

    def test_update_item_not_found(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test updating a non-existent item returns 404."""
        update_data = {"name": "Updated", "price": 15.0}
        response = client.put("/items/999", json=update_data)
        assert response.status_code == 404
        assert response.json()["detail"] == "Item not found"

    def test_delete_item(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test deleting an item."""
        # Create an item first
        item_data = {"name": "To Delete", "price": 10.0}
        create_response = client.post("/items", json=item_data)
        item_id = create_response.json()["id"]

        # Delete it
        response = client.delete(f"/items/{item_id}")
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.json()["message"] == "Item deleted successfully"

        # Verify it is gone
        get_response = client.get(f"/items/{item_id}")
        assert get_response.status_code == 404

    def test_delete_item_not_found(self, client: TestClient):
        """Test deleting a non-existent item returns 404."""
        response = client.delete("/items/999")
        assert response.status_code == 404
        assert response.json()["detail"] == "Item not found"

# FUNCTIONAL PROGRAMMING RESEARCH SUMMARY
## Core Concepts

### 1. Pure Functions
- Output depends ONLY on inputs (no side effects)
- Same input → Same output (referential transparency)
- No mutation of external state

### 2. Immutability
- Data cannot be modified after creation
- Changes create new data structures
- Prevents bugs from unexpected mutations

### 3. First-Class & Higher-Order Functions
- Functions are values (can be assigned, passed, returned)
- Higher-order functions: accept/return functions
- Examples: map, filter, reduce, compose

### 4. Function Composition
- Combining simple functions to build complex logic
- Creates pipelines: f(g(x))
- Point-free/tacit programming style

### 5. Declarative vs Imperative
- WHAT to do vs HOW to do it
- Focus on transformations, not step-by-step instructions

## Key Patterns
- Pattern Matching (case/destructuring)
- Recursion (instead of loops)
- Lazy Evaluation (on-demand computation)
- Monads (Maybe, Either, IO for side effects)
- Currying & Partial Application

## Paradigm Languages
- Haskell (pure functional)
- Lisp/Scheme/Clojure
- Erlang/Elixir
- Scala, F#
- JavaScript (functional capabilities)
- Python (functional features)

## Benefits
- Easier testing & debugging
- Concurrent/parallel-friendly
- More predictable code
- Better modularity
EOF

cat << 'EOF'
# K-means Clustering Summary

## Algorithm Overview:
K-means is an unsupervised machine learning algorithm for clustering data into K groups.

## How it works:
1. **Initialization**: Randomly select K data points as initial centroids
2. **Assignment**: Assign each data point to the nearest centroid (using Euclidean distance)
3. **Update**: Recalculate centroids as the mean of all points assigned to each cluster
4. **Repeat**: Steps 2-3 until convergence (centroids stop changing or max iterations reached)

## Key Properties:
- Time complexity: O(n * K * I * d) where:
  - n = number of data points
  - K = number of clusters
  - I = number of iterations
  - d = number of dimensions
- Space complexity: O(n * d + K * d)
- Distance metric: Typically Euclidean distance
- Objective: Minimize within-cluster sum of squares (WCSS)

## Limitations:
- Requires specifying K in advance
- Sensitive to initial centroid selection
- Assumes spherical clusters
- Struggles with clusters of different sizes/densities

## Use Cases:
- Customer segmentation
- Image compression (vector quantization)
- Document clustering
- Anomaly detection
EOF

import asyncio
import random
import aiohttp


async def fetch_url(session, url):
    """Fetch a URL asynchronously."""
    async with session.get(url) as response:
        return await response.text()


async def gather_example():
    """Example of gather for concurrent execution."""
    urls = [
        'https://httpbin.org/get',
        'https://httpbin.org/delay/1',
        'https://httpbin.org/delay/2',
    ]
    
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        tasks = [fetch_url(session, url) for url in urls]
        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        return results


async def semaphore_example():
    """Rate limiting with semaphore."""
    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(5)  # Max 5 concurrent
    
    async def limited_task(task_id):
        async with semaphore:
            await asyncio.sleep(random.uniform(0.1, 0.5))
            return f"Task {task_id} completed"
    
    tasks = [limited_task(i) for i in range(20)]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

"""
Rate limiting and throttling patterns.
"""
import asyncio
import time
from collections import deque
from functools import wraps


class RateLimiter:
    """Token bucket rate limiter."""
    
    def __init__(self, rate, period=1.0):
        self.rate = rate
        self.period = period
        self.tokens = rate
        self.updated_at = time.monotonic()
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()
    
    async def acquire(self):
        async with self._lock:
            now = time.monotonic()
            elapsed = now - self.updated_at
            self.tokens = min(self.rate, self.tokens + elapsed * self.rate / self.period)
            self.updated_at = now
            
            if self.tokens < 1:
                wait_time = (1 - self.tokens) * self.period / self.rate
                await asyncio.sleep(wait_time)
                self.tokens = 0
            else:
                self.tokens -= 1
            
            return True


def rate_limited(rate, period=1.0):
    """Decorator for rate limiting."""
    limiter = RateLimiter(rate, period)
    
    def decorator(func):
        @wraps(func)
        async def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            await limiter.acquire()
            return await func(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper
    return decorator


class AsyncThrottler:
    """Simple async throttler."""
    
    def __init__(self, max_concurrent):
        self.semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
    
    async def __aenter__(self):
        await self.semaphore.acquire()
        return self
    
    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        self.semaphore.release()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Rate limiting patterns loaded")
EOF

# ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused - Common Solutions (from Stack Overflow and official Python docs)

## What causes ConnectionRefusedError (Errno 111)?

1. **Server is not running**: The server process hasn't started or crashed
2. **Wrong port number**: Connecting to a port the server isn't listening on
3. **Firewall blocking connection**: Network/firewall blocking the port
4. **Wrong host/IP address**: Connecting to the wrong machine
5. **Server backlog full**: Server's connection queue is full
6. **Socket timeout**: Connection attempt timed out

## Common Solutions:

### 1. Check if server is running ( diagnose first )
```bash
netstat -tlnp | grep <port>  # Linux
# or
lsof -i :<port>             # macOS/Linux
```

### 2. Add retry logic with exponential backoff
```python
import socket
import time

def connect_with_retry(host, port, max_retries=5):
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        try:
            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            sock.connect((host, port))
            return sock
        except ConnectionRefusedError:
            if attempt < max_retries - 1:
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)  # exponential backoff
            else:
                raise
```

### 3. Check server availability before connecting
```python
import socket

def is_port_open(host, port, timeout=5):
    try:
        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
            return True
    except (socket.error, ConnectionRefusedError):
        return False
```

### 4. Handle the error gracefully
```python
try:
    socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=10)
except ConnectionRefusedError as e:
    print(f"Server not available: {e}")
    # Handle graceful degradation
```

### 5. For HTTP requests (using requests library)
```python
import requests
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter, Retry

session = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=1, status_forcelist=[502, 503, 504])
session.mount('http://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
```

### 6. For databases/lots of connections - verify connection pool settings
```python
import psycopg2.pool
# Use connection pooling to manage resources
pool = psycopg2.pool.ThreadedConnectionPool(minconn=1, maxconn=10, ...)
```

### 7. For Docker containers - check exposed ports
```yaml

      - "127.0.0.1:5000:5000"  # explicit bind
```

## Executive Summary

This report compiles industry-standard best practices for designing robust, scalable, and maintainable APIs. The recommendations are based on widely adopted standards including RFC specifications, industry leaders (Google, Microsoft, Stripe, GitHub), and modern API design patterns.

## 1. REST API Design Fundamentals

### 1.1 Resource Naming Conventions

Use nouns, not verbs, to represent resources:
```
✅ GET /users          ❌ GET /getUsers
✅ POST /tasks         ❌ POST /createTask
✅ GET /orders/{id}    ❌ GET /getOrderById/{id}
```

**Naming Rules:**
- Use plural nouns for collections: `/users`, `/orders`, `/products`
- Use kebab-case for multi-word resources: `/order-items`
- Use lowercase consistently
- Nest for relationships: `/users/{id}/orders`, `/orders/{id}/items`
- Keep URLs as flat as possible (max 3-4 levels deep)

### 1.2 HTTP Methods Usage

| Method | Purpose | Idempotent | Safe |
|--------|---------|------------|------|
| GET | Retrieve resource(s) | Yes | Yes |
| POST | Create new resource | No | No |
| PUT | Full update/replace | Yes | No |
| PATCH | Partial update | No* | No |
| DELETE | Remove resource | Yes | No |

**Examples:**
```http
GET    /api/v1/users          # List users
GET    /api/v1/users/123      # Get specific user
POST   /api/v1/users          # Create new user
PUT    /api/v1/users/123      # Replace user entirely
PATCH  /api/v1/users/123      # Update specific fields
DELETE /api/v1/users/123      # Delete user
```

### 1.3 HTTP Status Codes

**Success (2xx):**
- `200 OK` - Standard success response
- `201 Created` - Resource created successfully
- `202 Accepted` - Request accepted for async processing
- `204 No Content` - Success, no body to return

**Client Errors (4xx):**
- `400 Bad Request` - Invalid request syntax
- `401 Unauthorized` - Authentication required
- `403 Forbidden` - No permission to access
- `404 Not Found` - Resource doesn't exist
- `409 Conflict` - Resource conflict (e.g., duplicate)
- `422 Unprocessable Entity` - Validation errors
- `429 Too Many Requests` - Rate limit exceeded

**Server Errors (5xx):**
- `500 Internal Server Error` - Unexpected server error
- `502 Bad Gateway` - Invalid response from upstream
- `503 Service Unavailable` - Server temporarily unavailable

### 1.4 API Versioning Strategies

**URL Path Versioning (Recommended):**
```
/api/v1/users
/api/v2/users
```

**Header Versioning:**
```http
Accept: application/vnd.api+json;version=2
X-API-Version: 2
```

**Best Practices:**
- Start with v1
- Maintain backward compatibility when possible
- Deprecate old versions with notice (6-12 months)
- Document version differences

### 1.5 Pagination Patterns

**Offset-based (Page/Offset):**
```http
GET /api/v1/users?page=2&per_page=20
GET /api/v1/users?offset=40&limit=20
```

**Cursor-based (Recommended for large datasets):**
```http
GET /api/v1/users?cursor=abc123&limit=20
```

**Response Format:**
```json
{
  "data": [...],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 2,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total": 100,
    "total_pages": 5,
    "has_next": true,
    "has_prev": true
  },
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v1/users?page=2",
    "first": "/api/v1/users?page=1",
    "prev": "/api/v1/users?page=1",
    "next": "/api/v1/users?page=3",
    "last": "/api/v1/users?page=5"
  }
}
```

Default to 20 items per page, max 100.

## 2. Authentication and Security

### 2.1 OAuth 2.0 / JWT

**JWT Token Structure:**
```json
{
  "header": {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"},
  "payload": {
    "sub": "user123",
    "iat": 1704067200,
    "exp": 1706659200,
    "scope": "read write"
  },
  "signature": "..."
}
```

**Best Practices:**
- Use HTTPS only (TLS 1.2+)
- Short expiration for access tokens (15-60 min)
- Use refresh tokens for long-term sessions (days/weeks)
- Store tokens securely (HttpOnly cookies preferred)
- Include scope/permissions in token
- Validate signature on every request

### 2.2 API Keys

```http
GET /api/v1/data
Authorization: ApiKey abc123xyz789
X-API-Key: abc123xyz789
```

- Use for server-to-server communication
- Rotate keys regularly
- Support multiple keys per account
- Provide key usage monitoring

### 2.3 Rate Limiting

**Headers to Include:**
```http
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 999
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1640995200
```

**Rate Limit Response (429):**
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Too many requests. Try again at 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

**Strategies:**
- Per-user limits (authenticated)
- Per-IP limits (unauthenticated)
- Different tiers (free, pro, enterprise)

### 2.4 CORS Configuration

```javascript
// Express CORS example
app.use(cors({
  origin: ['https://myapp.com', 'https://admin.myapp.com'],
  methods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  allowedHeaders: ['Content-Type', 'Authorization'],
  credentials: true
}));
```

### 2.5 Security Checklist
- [ ] Use HTTPS everywhere
- [ ] Validate and sanitize all inputs
- [ ] Prevent SQL/NoSQL injection
- [ ] Use parameterized queries
- [ ] Implement proper CORS
- [ ] Set security headers (HSTS, CSP)
- [ ] Log security events
- [ ] Implement request size limits
- [ ] Add timeout configurations

---

## 3. Request and Response Design

### 3.1 JSON Schema Best Practices

**Consistent Envelope:**
```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "meta": { ... },
  "links": { ... }
}
```

**Date/Time Formats:**
- Use ISO 8601: `2024-01-15T10:30:00Z`
- Include timezone or use UTC
- Be consistent across API

**Naming Conventions:**
- camelCase for JavaScript APIs
- snake_case for Python/Ruby APIs
- Be consistent within the API

### 3.2 Error Response Format

**Standard Error Structure:**
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "The request failed validation",
    "details": [
      {
        "field": "email",
        "message": "Invalid email format"
      },
      {
        "field": "password",
        "message": "Must be at least 8 characters"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Error Codes:**
- VALIDATION_ERROR
- AUTHENTICATION_ERROR
- AUTHORIZATION_ERROR
- RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND
- RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

### 3.3 Filtering, Sorting, Searching

**Filtering:**
```http
GET /api/v1/tasks?status=active&priority=high
GET /api/v1/tasks?created_after=2024-01-01
GET /api/v1/users?role[in]=admin,moderator
```

**Sorting:**
```http
GET /api/v1/tasks?sort=-created_at,+priority
# - prefix = descending, + or no prefix = ascending
```

**Searching:**
```http
GET /api/v1/users?q=john
GET /api/v1/products?search=laptop gaming
```

**Field Selection:**
```http
GET /api/v1/users?fields=id,name,email
GET /api/v1/users?exclude=password,internal_notes
```

### 3.4 Content Negotiation

```http
Accept: application/json
Accept: application/xml
Accept-Language: en-US
Accept-Encoding: gzip
```

Return `406 Not Acceptable` if format not supported.

## 4. Documentation Standards

### 4.1 OpenAPI/Swagger Specification

**Benefits:**
- Interactive documentation
- Code generation
- Automated testing
- Client SDK generation

**Best Practices:**
- Document all endpoints
- Include request/response examples
- Define all possible error responses
- Tag and categorize endpoints
- Include authentication requirements
- Version your spec alongside API

**Example Structure:**
```yaml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: My API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /users:
    get:
      summary: List users
      parameters:
        - name: page
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        200:
          description: Successful response
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/UserList'
```

### 4.2 API Documentation Tools

- **Swagger UI** - Interactive docs
- **ReDoc** - Clean, responsive docs
- **Stoplight** - Design-first platform
- **Postman** - Collection-based docs
- **ReadMe** - Developer experience platform

---

## 5. Modern API Patterns

### 5.1 GraphQL Considerations

**When to Use:**
- Mobile apps with varying data needs
- Complex data relationships
- Need for precise data fetching

**When NOT to Use:**
- Simple CRUD operations
- File upload-heavy APIs
- When caching is critical

### 5.2 gRPC

**When to Use:**
- Microservices communication
- High-performance requirements
- Polyglot environments

**Trade-offs:**
- Binary protocol (harder to debug)
- Requires HTTP/2
- Less browser support

### 5.3 Webhooks

**Best Practices:**
- Sign payloads for verification
- Implement retry with exponential backoff
- Allow endpoint configuration
- Provide event types filtering
- Include event ID for idempotency

**Example Payload:**
```json
{
  "id": "evt_123456",
  "type": "user.created",
  "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "data": {
    "user_id": "user_789",
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }
}
```

### 5.4 AsyncAPI

Use AsyncAPI for event-driven architectures:
- Document WebSocket APIs
- Message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ)
- Event-driven microservices

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
HuggingFace Hub Skill for finding and downloading models.
"""

import os
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
from huggingface_hub import HfApi, list_models, model_info, hf_hub_download, snapshot_download
from huggingface_hub.utils import RepositoryNotFoundError

class HuggingFaceHubSkill:
    """Skill for interacting with the HuggingFace Hub."""
    
    def __init__(self, token: Optional[str] = None):
        """Initialize the skill with optional authentication token."""
        self.api = HfApi(token=token)
        
    def search_models(
        self, 
        query: str = "", 
        task: Optional[str] = None, 
        language: Optional[str] = None,
        limit: int = 10,
        sort: str = "downloads"
    ) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Search for models on HuggingFace Hub.
        
        Args:
            query: Search query string
            task: Task filter (e.g., 'text-generation', 'fill-mask')
            language: Language filter (e.g., 'en', 'python')
            limit: Maximum number of results
            sort: Sort by 'downloads', 'likes', 'last_modified'
            
        Returns:
            List of model information dictionaries
        """
        print(f"🔍 Searching for models: query='{query}', task='{task}', limit={limit}")
        
        # Build search filter
        filter_kwargs = {}
        if task:
            filter_kwargs["pipeline_tag"] = task
            
        models = list_models(
            search=query,
            sort=sort,
            limit=limit,
            **filter_kwargs
        )
        
        results = []
        for model in models:
            info = {
                "model_id": model.modelId,
                "downloads": getattr(model, 'downloads', 'N/A'),
                "likes": getattr(model, 'likes', 'N/A'),
                "task": getattr(model, 'pipeline_tag', 'N/A'),
                "author": model.modelId.split('/')[0] if '/' in model.modelId else 'Unknown',
                "tags": getattr(model, 'tags', []),
                "last_modified": getattr(model, 'last_modified', 'N/A')
            }
            results.append(info)
            
        return results
    
    def get_model_info(self, model_id: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Get detailed information about a specific model.
        
        Args:
            model_id: Full model ID (e.g., 'microsoft/CodeGPT-small-py')
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with model information
        """
        try:
            info = model_info(model_id)
            return {
                "model_id": info.modelId,
                "downloads": getattr(info, 'downloads', 0),
                "likes": getattr(info, 'likes', 0),
                "task": getattr(info, 'pipeline_tag', 'N/A'),
                "tags": getattr(info, 'tags', []),
                "description": getattr(info, 'cardData', {}).get('description', 'No description available'),
                "license": getattr(info, 'cardData', {}).get('license', 'Unknown')
            }
        except RepositoryNotFoundError:
            print(f"❌ Model '{model_id}' not found on HuggingFace Hub")
            return {}
    
    def download_model(
        self, 
        model_id: str, 
        local_dir: Optional[str] = None,
        allow_patterns: Optional[List[str]] = None
    ) -> str:
        """
        Download a model from HuggingFace Hub.
        
        Args:
            model_id: Full model ID
            local_dir: Local directory to download to (default: ./models/{model_id})
            allow_patterns: Patterns of files to download (e.g., ['*.json', '*.bin'])
            
        Returns:
            Path to the downloaded model directory
        """
        if local_dir is None:
            local_dir = os.path.join("./models", model_id.replace("/", "_"))
            
        os.makedirs(local_dir, exist_ok=True)
        
        print(f"📥 Downloading model: {model_id}")
        print(f"📁 Destination: {local_dir}")
        
        try:
            # Use snapshot_download for downloading all model files
            downloaded_path = snapshot_download(
                repo_id=model_id,
                local_dir=local_dir,
                allow_patterns=allow_patterns,
                resume_download=True
            )
            print(f"✅ Model downloaded successfully to: {downloaded_path}")
            return downloaded_path
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ Error downloading model: {e}")
            raise
    
    def download_file(
        self, 
        model_id: str, 
        filename: str,
        local_dir: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> str:
        """
        Download a specific file from a model repository.
        
        Args:
            model_id: Full model ID
            filename: Name of the file to download
            local_dir: Local directory to download to
            
        Returns:
            Path to the downloaded file
        """
        if local_dir:
            os.makedirs(local_dir, exist_ok=True)
            
        print(f"📥 Downloading file: {filename} from {model_id}")
        
        try:
            file_path = hf_hub_download(
                repo_id=model_id,
                filename=filename,
                local_dir=local_dir,
                resume_download=True
            )
            print(f"✅ File downloaded: {file_path}")
            return file_path
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ Error downloading file: {e}")
            raise


def main():
    """Example usage of the HuggingFace Hub Skill."""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Task 1: Analyze Code Quality
Analyzes the legacy codebase for quality issues, anti-patterns, and technical debt.
"""

import ast
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path


class CodeQualityAnalyzer:
    def __init__(self, codebase_path):
        self.codebase_path = codebase_path
        self.issues = []
        self.metrics = {}
        
    def analyze(self):
        """Run all code quality checks"""
        print("=" * 60)
        print("TASK 1: CODE QUALITY ANALYSIS")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        for root, _, files in os.walk(self.codebase_path):
            for file in files:
                if file.endswith('.py'):
                    filepath = os.path.join(root, file)
                    self._analyze_file(filepath)
        
        self._generate_report()
        return self.issues, self.metrics
    
    def _analyze_file(self, filepath):
        """Analyze a single Python file"""
        with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
            content = f.read()
        
        # Syntax and structure analysis
        try:
            tree = ast.parse(content)
        except SyntaxError as e:
            self.issues.append(f"[ERROR] Syntax error in {filepath}: {e}")
            return
        
        # Security issues
        if 'eval(' in content:
            self.issues.append(f"[SECURITY] Use of eval() detected in {filepath} - major security risk")
        if 'password' in content.lower() and 'hash' not in content.lower():
            self.issues.append(f"[SECURITY] Possible plain-text password handling in {filepath}")
        
        # Code smells
        if content.count('global ') > 0:
            self.issues.append(f"[CODE_SMELL] Global variables used in {filepath}")
        if 'time.sleep' in content:
            self.issues.append(f"[PERFORMANCE] Blocking sleep() calls in {filepath}")
        
        # Count lines and functions
        lines = content.split('\n')
        functions = [node.name for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)]
        classes = [node.name for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef)]
        
        self.metrics[filepath] = {
            'lines': len(lines),
            'functions': len(functions),
            'classes': len(classes),
            'function_names': functions,
            'class_names': classes
        }
    
    def _generate_report(self):
        """Generate final report"""
        print("\n📊 CODE QUALITY REPORT")
        print("-" * 50)
        print(f"Total Issues Found: {len(self.issues)}")
        print(f"Files Analyzed: {len(self.metrics)}")
        
        total_lines = sum(m['lines'] for m in self.metrics.values())
        print(f"Total Lines of Code: {total_lines}")
        
        if self.issues:
            print("\n⚠️  ISSUES BREAKDOWN:")
            categories = {}
            for issue in self.issues:
                cat = issue[1:].split(']')[0]
                categories[cat] = categories.get(cat, 0) + 1
            for cat, count in sorted(categories.items()):
                print(f"  - {cat}: {count}")
            
            print("\n📝 DETAILED ISSUES:")
            for issue in self.issues:
                print(f"  {issue}")
        else:
            print("\n✅ No major issues found")
        
        print("\n📈 METRICS:")
        for filepath, metrics in self.metrics.items():
            print(f"  {filepath}:")
            print(f"    Lines: {metrics['lines']}, Functions: {metrics['functions']}, Classes: {metrics['classes']}")
            if metrics['function_names']:
                print(f"    Functions: {', '.join(metrics['function_names'][:5])}" + ("..." if len(metrics['function_names']) > 5 else ""))
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    analyzer = CodeQualityAnalyzer("/root/sample_project")
    analyzer.analyze()

# PageRank Algorithm Research

## Overview
PageRank is an algorithm used by Google Search to rank web pages in their search engine results. It was named after Larry Page, one of the founders of Google. The algorithm measures the importance of website pages by counting the number and quality of links to a page.

## Key Concepts

### 1. Basic Idea
- Pages with more backlinks (incoming links) are more important
- Links from important pages carry more weight
- The algorithm models a "random surfer" who clicks links randomly

### 2. Mathematical Formulation
The PageRank of a page $u$ is defined as:

$$PR(u) = \frac{1-d}{N} + d \sum_{v \in B_u} \frac{PR(v)}{L(v)}$$

Where:
- $PR(u)$ = PageRank of page $u$
- $N$ = Total number of pages
- $d$ = Damping factor (typically 0.85)
- $B_u$ = Set of pages linking to $u$
- $L(v)$ = Number of outbound links from page $v$
- $\frac{1-d}{N}$ = Probability of jumping to any random page

### 3. Matrix Formulation
Can be expressed as an eigenvalue problem:

$$\mathbf{r} = dM\mathbf{r} + \frac{1-d}{N}\mathbf{1}$$

Where $M$ is the column-stochastic matrix of the web graph.

### 4. Damping Factor
- Typical value: 0.85
- Represents probability of continuing to follow links vs. jumping randomly
- Ensures convergence and handles dangling nodes (pages with no outgoing links)

## Implementation Approaches

### 1. Power Iteration Method
- Iteratively compute PR values until convergence
- Time complexity: O(k * E) where k = iterations, E = edges
- Most practical for large graphs

### 2. Algebraic Method
- Solve linear system directly
- O(N³) complexity - impractical for large graphs

### 3. Monte Carlo Method
- Simulate random walks
- Useful for approximate results on very large graphs

## Convergence Criteria
- Stop when L1 norm of change < ε (typically 1e-6 to 1e-8)
- Or maximum number of iterations reached

## Variants

### 1. Personalized PageRank
- Biased teleportation to specific nodes
- Used for recommendations

### 2. Topic-Sensitive PageRank
- Different teleportation for different query topics

## Properties
- Sums to 1 (probability distribution)
- Converges for strongly connected graphs
- Handles dangling nodes via teleportation

## Complexity
- Space: O(N + E)
- Time per iteration: O(E)
- Convergence: Usually < 100 iterations for reasonable ε
EOF

apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: user-api-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: user-api
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: memory
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 80
'''

# GitHub Actions workflow
github_workflow = '''name: CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: '3.11'
    
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt
    
    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        pip install pytest pytest-cov
        pytest --cov=. test_app.py
    
    - name: Lint with flake8
      run: |
        pip install flake8
        flake8 . --count --select=E9,F63,F7,F82 --show-source --statistics

  build-and-push:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Build Docker image
      run: docker build -t user-api:${{ github.sha }} .
    
    - name: Login to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v2
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
    
    - name: Push to Docker Hub
      run: |
        docker tag user-api:${{ github.sha }} ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/user-api:${{ github.sha }}
        docker tag user-api:${{ github.sha }} ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/user-api:latest
        docker push ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/user-api:${{ github.sha }}
        docker push ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/user-api:latest

  deploy:
    needs: build-and-push
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
      run: |
        kubectl set image deployment/user-api user-api=${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/user-api:${{ github.sha }}
        kubectl rollout status deployment/user-api
'''

    kmeans_lloyd = KMeans(k=k, use_elkan=False, random_state=42)

    results = []

@dataclass
class Event:
    event_id: str
    timestamp: float
    aggregate_id: str
    event_type: str
    data: dict
    version: int

class EventStore:
    def __init__(self):
        self.events: List[Event] = []
        self.subscribers: List[callable] = []
        self.aggregate_versions: Dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    
    def append(self, aggregate_id: str, event_type: str, data: dict) -> Event:
        self.aggregate_versions[aggregate_id] += 1
        event = Event(
            event_id=f"evt_{len(self.events)}",
            timestamp=time.time(),
            aggregate_id=aggregate_id,
            event_type=event_type,
            data=data,
            version=self.aggregate_versions[aggregate_id]
        )
        self.events.append(event)
        self._notify_subscribers(event)
        return event
    
    def subscribe(self, callback: callable):
        self.subscribers.append(callback)
    
    def _notify_subscribers(self, event: Event):
        for subscriber in self.subscribers:
            subscriber(event)
    
    def get_events_for_aggregate(self, aggregate_id: str) -> List[Event]:
        return [e for e in self.events if e.aggregate_id == aggregate_id]
    
    def rebuild_from_events(self, projection: callable):
        state = {}
        for event in self.events:
            state = projection(state, event)
        return state

class BankAccount:
    def __init__(self, account_id: str, event_store: EventStore):
        self.account_id = account_id
        self.event_store = event_store
        self.balance = 0
    
    def deposit(self, amount: float):
        self.event_store.append(self.account_id, "MoneyDeposited", {"amount": amount})
    
    def withdraw(self, amount: float):
        if amount > self.balance:
            events = self.event_store.get_events_for_aggregate(self.account_id)
            self.balance = 0
            for event in events:
                if event.event_type == "MoneyDeposited":
                    self.balance += event.data["amount"]
                elif event.event_type == "MoneyWithdrawn":
                    self.balance -= event.data["amount"]
        if amount > self.balance:
            raise ValueError(f"Insufficient funds. Current balance: ${self.balance}")
        self.event_store.append(self.account_id, "MoneyWithdrawn", {"amount": amount})
    
    def rebuild_from_events(self):
        events = self.event_store.get_events_for_aggregate(self.account_id)
        self.balance = 0
        for event in events:
            if event.event_type == "MoneyDeposited":
                self.balance += event.data["amount"]
            elif event.event_type == "MoneyWithdrawn":
                self.balance -= event.data["amount"]
        return self.balance

class GCounter:
    """Grow-Only Counter CRDT"""
    def __init__(self, replica_id: str):
        self.replica_id = replica_id
        self.p = defaultdict(int)
    
    def increment(self):
        self.p[self.replica_id] += 1
        return self
    
    def query(self) -> int:
        return sum(self.p.values())
    
    def merge(self, other: 'GCounter') -> 'GCounter':
        result = GCounter(self.replica_id)
        all_replicas = set(self.p.keys()) | set(other.p.keys())
        for replica in all_replicas:
            result.p[replica] = max(self.p.get(replica, 0), other.p.get(replica, 0))
        return result
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"GCounter({self.replica_id}): {dict(self.p)} = {self.query()}"

class PNCounter:
    """Positive-Negative Counter CRDT"""
    def __init__(self, replica_id: str):
        self.replica_id = replica_id
        self.p = GCounter(f"{replica_id}_p")
        self.n = GCounter(f"{replica_id}_n")
    
    def increment(self):
        self.p.increment()
        return self
    
    def decrement(self):
        self.n.increment()
        return self
    
    def query(self) -> int:
        return self.p.query() - self.n.query()
    
    def merge(self, other: 'PNCounter') -> 'PNCounter':
        result = PNCounter(self.replica_id)
        result.p = self.p.merge(other.p)
        result.n = self.n.merge(other.n)
        return result
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"PNCounter({self.replica_id}): {self.query()} (+{self.p.query()}, -{self.n.query()})"
